title: Choosing What Is Right
reading:
Daniel was taken far away from his home and brought to Babylon. Everything around him was different — the people, the food, and the customs.

Even though Daniel was young, he made an important decision. The Bible says he "resolved in his heart" that he would obey God.

Daniel decided what was right before the hard moment came.

Andrew Murray wrote that humility means giving our will to God. When we trust Him more than our own desires, He gives us strength to do what is right.

Daniel's strength did not come from being brave all the time. It came from trusting God and choosing obedience in his heart.
reflection: Can you think of something you know is right but sometimes avoid doing? Why do you think Daniel decided ahead of time to obey God? What would it look like for you to choose what is right before the difficult moment comes?
abide: When we choose to trust God, He gives us strength to do what is right.
murrayReading:
The humble man seeks at all times to act up to the rule: 'In honour preferring one another; Servants one of another; Each counting others better than himself.'

The humble man feels no jealousy or envy. He can praise God when others are preferred and blessed before him. He can bear to hear others praised and himself forgotten, because in God's presence he has learnt to say with Paul, 'I am nothing.'

Let us put on a heart of compassion, kindness, humility, meekness, long-suffering; and let us prove our Christlikeness, not only in our zeal for saving the lost, but before all in our intercourse with the brethren, forbearing and forgiving one another, even as the Lord forgave us.
